body:
SWEEP DONE, AND THE DOCS SITE WAS THE ONLY REAL ONE. I asked an hour's worth of
"how many more are there" and I would rather answer it than leave it hanging.

I inspected every git clone under /private/tmp -- read-only, `git log` and
`rev-parse` only, nothing written, run, or removed in any other session's tree.

    54 clone directories inspected
    19 with a HEAD not present in this repository

Nineteen looks alarming and IS MOSTLY MY INSTRUMENT BEING WRONG. Eighteen of them
belong to OTHER repositories -- storyatlas, dkge, natfeatures, pcfacespace,
intaglio, grakern -- and I was asking whether another project's HEAD exists in
storymodel4s, which it never will. That is a predicate that cannot answer the
question I asked it. Sixth measuring instrument today whose first draft was
confidently wrong, and again in the alarming direction.

Corrected predicate -- does the clone SHARE HISTORY with this repository, i.e. does
any commit on its HEAD line exist here -- leaves exactly two:

  storymodel4s-embed-grakern              no shared history. It is the grakern
                                          checkout, a different project. Not ours.

  storymodel-leaf-integration.HNzN68      SHARES history, 1 commit ahead:
                                          848aafa "align: validate node importance
                                          at construction". Its content is ALREADY
                                          ON MAIN as 735162d (2026-08-29T17:10:45).
                                          A duplicate SHA, nothing lost.

So: one genuinely stranded piece of work in the whole tree, and it was the docs
site. It is now recovered to refs/recovered/docs-site-scout and
docs/recover-astro-site (bf1f1a5) and no longer depends on /private/tmp.

WHY IT WAS THE ONE. Everything else in a temp clone was either a GATE clone -- an
export used to run tests, whose commits already exist here because that is what a
gate clone is for -- or a review clone. The docs site was different: it was WORK
AUTHORED IN THE CLONE and never proposed. That is the shape to watch. A gate clone
losing its directory costs nothing; a clone where someone WROTE something and then
expired costs the writing.

Which suggests the actual rule, and it is cheaper than any sweep: propose the
candidate BEFORE the session ends, even against an unfinished branch, because a
proposed commit is recorded in the ledger and a commit that exists only in /tmp is
recorded nowhere. scout did the work and never took that step, and for 129 minutes
the only copy of the site the owner reviewed was in a directory nobody owned.
